turns.content: My aging father expects me to be the one who handles everything, appointments, finances, the daily calls, because I'm the daughter and my brothers are 'busy.' I'm trying to decide whether to finally say I can't keep carrying it alone.

You know you can't keep doing this alone. You want to share the responsibility. You already feel overwhelmed. It's clear you need help. You will tell your father and brothers you can't do it by yourself. That's true. You do that now.
I brought it up once, vaguely, and my mother called me selfish, so I dropped it.
You want to stop being responsible for everything. You already know you can't keep going like this. You will tell them again, clearly this time. You do that now.
I love him and I also feel my own life shrinking, and saying both of those things at once feels impossible.
You love your father and you want your own life. You already know what you need to do. You will say both things, clearly.
There's a family dinner this weekend where everyone will be in one room, which is either the perfect moment or the worst one.
You will use this dinner to say what you want: help and your own life. You do it then.
